integration_issues.flow: Evidence Locker — Anchor & verify (needs signal) on web
integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL, STILL BROKEN (third distinct root cause, same end-user symptom). Exact status-text/error captured VERBATIM from the live UI: "(0 , _evidenceStore.readEncryptedBytes) is not a function". Root cause: `readEncryptedBytes` was added as an export ONLY to /app/frontend/src/women/evidenceStore.ts (the native/default module), but NOT to /app/frontend/src/women/evidenceStore.web.ts — the platform-specific file that Metro's web bundler resolves INSTEAD of evidenceStore.ts whenever the app runs on web (standard React Native platform-extension resolution: a `.web.ts` sibling always wins over `.ts` for web builds). evidenceBackup.ts does `import { readEncryptedBytes, type RecordingItem } from './evidenceStore'` — on web this import resolves to evidenceStore.web.ts, where `readEncryptedBytes` simply does not exist (confirmed by viewing the file in full — it has no such export), so it is `undefined` at call time, producing the exact TypeError captured above the instant anchorItem() tries to invoke it.

react_native_issues.issue: No red-screen crash, confirmed again — the error is caught by evidence-locker.tsx's doAnchor() try/catch and shown as readable status text. Error handling remains solid; only the underlying implementation (now a missing export on web) is broken.

action_items: CRITICAL — add a `readEncryptedBytes(item: RecordingItem): Promise<Uint8Array>` export to /app/frontend/src/women/evidenceStore.web.ts. It is currently completely missing from that file, causing the captured 'readEncryptedBytes is not a function' TypeError on web. This file is the one Metro actually resolves for web builds, NOT evidenceStore.ts — the fix applied before this test only touched the latter.

IMPORTANT — the web implementation CANNOT reuse the `new File(item.uri).bytes()` pattern (the one used in evidenceStore.ts's version) because on web, RecordingItem.uri is intentionally ALWAYS an empty string ('') — see the type comment at the top of evidenceStore.web.ts: ciphertext lives only as an IndexedDB Blob, never as a file:// URI. The correct web-specific implementation must read the IndexedDB 'recordings' object store directly for the matching row and return its stored Blob's raw bytes, e.g.: `export async function readEncryptedBytes(item: RecordingItem): Promise<Uint8Array> { const rows = await transaction<Stored[]>('readonly', store => store.getAll()); const row = rows.find(r => r.id === item.id); if (!row) throw new Error('This item could not be found on this device anymore.'); return new Uint8Array(await row.blob.arrayBuffer()); }` — this mirrors the exact Blob-reading logic already proven working inside getDecryptedTempUri() in the same file (lines 68-77 of evidenceStore.web.ts), just returning raw ciphertext bytes instead of decrypting + creating a blob: URL.

Once fixed, retest the full chain (Anchor -> Backup -> Certificate -> GET /api/evidence/backups?scope=device) in ONE browser session per the sequence documented below — do not assume Backup/Certificate work just because Anchor is fixed; they were never runtime-exercised in any of the 3 prior iterations because Anchor always failed first, and backupItem()'s web branch calls this SAME missing function, so it will fail identically until this export exists.

Recommend main agent add a checklist step for this codebase: any new export added to evidenceStore.ts for use by evidenceBackup.ts/evidence-locker.tsx MUST be mirrored in evidenceStore.web.ts with a web-appropriate implementation, since the two files are independent re-implementations with no shared interface contract that TypeScript enforces across the platform split — this exact class of miss has now caused the regression found in this specific iteration.
critical_code_review_comments: evidenceStore.ts and evidenceStore.web.ts have no compile-time contract ensuring export parity — TypeScript does not fail the build when evidenceStore.web.ts omits an export present in evidenceStore.ts, because each file is only type-checked against its own call sites for the actively-targeted platform. This is the structural reason the same class of mistake (web module missing a function the shared evidenceBackup.ts calls) was possible here.

Good: the defensive try/catch at every call site (doAnchor, handleBackup, handleCertificate) continues to prevent red-screen crashes and surfaces a readable error string — this made RCA on this run fast and unambiguous.

Could not evaluate backupItem()'s web branch or its bytesToBase64() helper at runtime this round since anchorItem() fails first (same blocker as iterations 27/28) — once readEncryptedBytes exists on evidenceStore.web.ts, backupItem() will call the SAME missing function and fail identically; this is a single shared fix for both Anchor and Backup.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Full working onboarding sequence confirmed in this run (must be in ONE browser_automation call — fresh profile every call): 1) goto app root -> language screen -> click text 'Continue · जारी रखें', 2) consent screen -> click consent-age-adult, consent-terms-checkbox, consent-data-checkbox, consent-continue-button in that order, 3) click continue-as-guest-button, 4) this redirects to /consent?mode=update -> repeat step 2's 4 clicks again, 5) lands on /home. THEN goto /women/evidence-locker directly (don't navigate via UI tabs, direct URL works fine). PIN gate: fill evidence-pin-input with '1234', click evidence-pin-submit, then (confirm step appears) fill '1234' again, click evidence-pin-submit again -> unlocked. Record audio: call page.context.grant_permissions(['microphone']) BEFORE navigating to the app, then click evidence-record-toggle to start, wait ~3s, click evidence-record-toggle again to stop & save. CRITICAL PLAYWRIGHT NOTE: the location opt-in dialog triggered by tapping 'Anchor & verify' renders as a native window.confirm() on web (via crossAlert). Playwright auto-dismisses dialogs by default (treated as Cancel), which silently does nothing on this screen since crossAlert's mapping has no cancelBtn.onPress when neither button sets style:'cancel'. You MUST register `page.on('dialog', lambda dialog: dialog.accept())` BEFORE clicking the anchor button — accept() maps to crossAlert's primaryBtn (the non-cancel-styled button, i.e. 'Skip' in this case) — to actually trigger doAnchor(). Do not retest PIN/record/photo/video/share/delete further this round — confirmed passing again, unaffected by this change.
rca_of_issue: This is the THIRD distinct root cause behind the same user-visible failure (Anchor never completes on web) across 3 testing iterations. (1) raw Alert.alert() silently no-op'd on web — fixed with crossAlert (iteration 27). (2) `new File(uri).bytes()` throws 'this.validatePath is not a function' on web (expo-file-system's new File API has no web validatePath implementation) — fix attempt #1 switched to expo-file-system/legacy's FileSystem.readAsStringAsync, which itself has ZERO web implementation (ExponentFileSystemShim throws UnavailabilityError unconditionally on web) — reported, not fixed by testing agent (iteration 28). (3, THIS RUN): fix attempt #2 added a new `readEncryptedBytes()` helper to evidenceStore.ts reusing the proven-working `new File(item.uri).bytes()` pattern from getDecryptedTempUri() — but this reasoning only holds for the NATIVE evidenceStore.ts module. Metro's platform-extension resolution means evidenceBackup.ts's `import { readEncryptedBytes } from './evidenceStore'` resolves to evidenceStore.web.ts on web (confirmed: this file exists and is a complete independent re-implementation using IndexedDB, with its own RecordingItem type and its own getDecryptedTempUri — it does NOT re-export from or extend evidenceStore.ts in any way). Since readEncryptedBytes was never added to evidenceStore.web.ts, calling it on web throws 'readEncryptedBytes is not a function'. Captured verbatim via live UI test: recorded and saved an audio item -> tapped 'Anchor & verify (needs signal)' -> accepted the window.confirm dialog (simulating tapping 'Skip') -> evidence-status immediately showed exactly '(0 , _evidenceStore.readEncryptedBytes) is not a function'; recording-vault-status-* stayed 'Not anchored yet · timestamp proof is optional'; no backup/certificate buttons rendered (same blocked downstream state as iterations 27/28). Additionally — even once this export is added to evidenceStore.web.ts, it structurally CANNOT use the `new File(uri).bytes()` pattern at all on web, because evidenceStore.web.ts's RecordingItem.uri is ALWAYS an empty string by design (ciphertext is stored as an IndexedDB Blob, never as a file:// or blob: URI on the item itself). The correct web implementation must read the IndexedDB 'recordings' object store directly for the matching row and return its stored Blob's bytes (suggested code given in action_items), mirroring the existing getDecryptedTempUri() Blob-read logic in that same file rather than any File/FileSystem API — this has now been true across all 3 fix attempts and should be the basis of fix attempt #3.
